course_summary:
ISEN 665 | Management of Engineering Systems | Spring 2026
Instructor: Michael Graul, PhD PE | mgraul@tamu.edu
Meets: M 5:45PM-8:15PM | ZACH 440
Grading: Quizzes [20%], Homework [20%], Midterm exam [30%], Project Work [30%] — A: {100 ≥ x ≥ 90}, B: {90 > x ≥ 80}, C: {80 > x ≥ 70}, D: {70 > x ≥ 60}, F: {60 > x}
Topics: IDEFO modeling, SysML, MBSE (Model-Based Systems Engineering), Systems Dynamics Modeling, Simulators for EM proficiency, Bias and Noise, MCS (Management Control Systems), CPM (Critical Path Method), PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique), CCPM (Critical Chain Project Management), NARD (Needs Analysis, Requirements Definition), SEMP (Systems Engineering Management Plan), STS (Socio-Technical Systems), HRO (High Reliability Organizations), managerial cybernetics, organization system design, earned value management, critical chain project management, complex system efforts management, system lifecycle management, technologically based systems management, socio-technical systems management, production systems management, apportionment of a system into projects, thrust areas, and programs, large system definition, system implementation, system execution, system sustainment, conceptualizing facets of the system, prescriptive methods, descriptive methods, models, conceptualizations, technical communication, life-cycle management of engineered systems, modern planning techniques, management of complex system, technology projects, organizational techniques, management control techniques, decision making techniques, life-cycle of technology programs, manage multi-role teams, communicate project status information, establish a cogent technical argument, problem definition, needs analysis, requirements definition, complex engineering system problem, Recitation, Application, Enriched Repetition, engineering system management, engineering management corpus, management techniques applied to engineered systems, complex technological systems, systems engineering, methods to represent complex systems, models to represent complex systems, characterize complex systems, interdependencies, knowledge, skills, and experiences (KSEs), experiential component, classroom exercises, management tools, concepting the system, quantitative forecasting, qualitative forecasting, deterministic decision making, stochastic decision making, system synthetic, Organizing, Controlling, R&D management, Production & Service System management, AI basics, AI-enabled management, Labor relations, Collective bargaining, project management controls, Agile project management, Systems engineering management, Risk management, Ethics, AI technology leveraging, AI-bot, prompt specification, AI generated material verification, literature review, leadership, management in engineering organizations, 'hard' skills, systems engineering process, project management, planning, forecasting, financial analysis, 'soft' skills, leadership styles, motivation, teamwork, managing creative people, navigating informal networks, science and technology policy, economic implications of engineering and technology, management functions (leading, controlling), contemporary support tools, practices
Tools: zoom, Canvas, Turnitin, AI technology
Prerequisites: Graduate classification
